body:

Who is supporting this ridiculousness? I mean they are only charging this coz apple fans are complicit.
[shxhshzhz] Exactly. Samsung S26 Ultra is only $1299 or $1234 price beat . Much cheaper and does most of the same things.
[miku] Not commenting about whether iPhones are worth $2K, or whether the S26 Ultra can/can't do most of what the iPhone can, but it's always been amusing to see with every release Samsung matching RRPs with Apple (e.g. S26 Ultra 256GB at $2199), but make avenues available to bring it down by up to 1/3rd before the phone's even out .
[krisspy] Because people are dumb and base purchases on rrp.
[BatmanAU] @montorola: Careful, you will upset all the neggers
[shegeloaf] Sa.sung are also trying to sell their phones at 2k. What jokes these companies are.
[onyx981] Memory and storage costs aside, a lot of companies seem to be basically testing the waters right now to see what people are willing to pay considering inflation doesn't seem to be affecting a good chunk of the population, especially people with paid off mortgages or ones comfortable racking up debt.
[He-Mania] Boomers buying $3k iphones?
My boomer parents had to reluctantly buy new iPhones because theirs were so grossly out of support and I don't want them getting a security exploit. They got the 14 series when the 16 came out I think.
Unless the boomers are tech savvy - most I know just want a phone to do the basic things - easy to use and take photos of thr grandkids and holidays
[greencomet] Because it has gone beyond being a phone and has become a status symbol. People love to spend money on something that makes them feel like they're better or more wealthy than someone else. They can make these 10 grand and people will still buy them, Apple owners don't care about the tech or features, they just care that it's expensive (and therefore the best) and that it makes them feel good/better than others with cheaper devices.
[SBOB] People love to spend money on something that makes them feel like they're better or more wealthy than someone else
One of the primary reasons new releases have new colours each year. Wouldn't want anyone thinking you're poor and using an out of date phone :)

So the the youngest is on 12 pro, older kid on 14 pro and my wife is on 16 pro. I'll buy the 18 pro and it goes down the chain. Each phone gets 6-7 years of use, which android phones struggle to achieve.
[shegeloaf] Your wrong. I am using my s10 which i bought in nov 2019 and also my note 10 + in 2020 is my 2nde phone.
I will use them another 3years. There is no need to upgrade really. Phones do the same as current phones. It's all marketting jargon.
[knockno] Android system updates and security patches, both stopped for s10 in 2023.
Comparatively the iPhone released in 2019 can get the latest iOS26 releasing this year and has been/will get security patches.
[Qazxswec] Tell that to my 7 year old samsung galaxy s10+ that still probably has a higher screen resolution than the iphone 18 pro max
[Stuj] Your idea of a kick ass theatre must wildly vary from me if you are talking about $1000 spare dollars, I’d like to see what that could get you (that is kick ass that is)
[QuickToThePointless] im talking about getting a basic smart phone, which can be had anywhere from $150, and spending the rest on something else that you use everyday.
3-4K gets you a decent amp/speaker setup that kicks the living sh*t out of the cast majority of peoples living room setups.
you could also wrangle a nice 55"+ OLED or 1080 projector into the mix if you are really on the bargain hunt.
treat the home theatre as a metaphor, and substitute it with any other of your hobbies and interests…
[gyrex] I hate to be that guy but "most everything" makes zero sense whatsoever. You're looking for *almost everything.
[QuickToThePointless] no worries friend - it's an abbreviation…sometimes I like to be "that guy" too…enjoy your evening!

[QuickToThePointless] a decent amp under 1K + 2K for sub and speakers will get you a very decent 2.1 system for movies and music that will work in pretty much any room.
it will certainly kick the ass of your sound bar.
and if you hunt the used market, you can make even a modest 1-2K budget go very, very far.
[TheFreaK] Wow guys if you spend 3k on speakers it’s better than 1k!

Glad you are being thorough though; feel free to put this exhange on your CV to boost your credentials - you can even list me as a reference!
[AustriaBargain] This is quite cheap really compared to what we used to pay for computers. The OLED display is good enough to watch a movie on, can watch 45 minutes of movie on a single charge, camera good enough to want to make nice prints of, more processing power than any other phone on the planet and most laptops. There is a lot to like and a lot of value.
[QuickToThePointless] really quite cheap compared to what we used to pay for computers?
now people are buying $5K phones and $5K PCs - and there is a lot of redundant functional overlap, obviously. i mean does anyone rationalise "i don't need PC any more - I just bought a $5K iphone; economically i am so far in front, suckers!"
lol @ watching a movie on your phone…and 45 mins no less? you don't work in sales, do you.
re: camera - billboard pixel quality prints sound great but standard photo frame size? phones maxxed out in practical terms to that end there several generations ago.
And you dont need enough processing power in your pocket to run a space station - people seem to forget that the primary function of these things is to send/receive SMS - emails/music/cameras/internet are a nice, convenient bonus - but all can be achieved with specs from over a decade ago.
[AustriaBargain] I meant 45 hours of video playback, not 45 minutes.
[QuickToThePointless] @AustriaBargain: i'd like to see that IRL…especially after a 6 months of battery use!
And my other points raised?
